original_question: Formulate a category of wild virtual knots together with an appropriate axiom system, and prove a criterion describing when a wild equivalence between tame virtual links already implies tame equivalence.
target_in_paper: Section 8.1, Problem 18 (“Wild virtuals”): “Create the category of ‘wild virtual knots’ and establish its axiomatics. In particular, one needs a theorem that states when a wild equivalence of tame virtual links implies a tame equivalence of these links.”
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s official formulation. It correctly identifies the two essential tasks in Problem 18: (1) define a category of wild virtual knots together with axioms, and (2) prove a criterion/theorem saying when a wild equivalence between tame virtual links already forces tame equivalence.
missing_details: The paper states this as Problem 18 in Section 8.1, i.e. an open problem in a problem list, not as a proved theorem or conjecture with an existing formal setup.

To be stand-alone, the question should specify the ambient virtual-link framework from Sections 2.1 and 2.3: virtual links are considered either as virtual link diagrams modulo generalized Reidemeister moves or, equivalently, as stable equivalence classes of links in thickened oriented surfaces.
The paper’s standard notion of stable equivalence should be included: isotopy in the thickened surfaces, homeomorphisms of the surfaces, and addition/removal of empty handles.

The wording should preserve the paper’s exact scope distinction: the new theory to be created is a category of “wild virtual knots,” but the theorem it asks for concerns when a wild equivalence of tame virtual links implies tame equivalence.

The paper does not define “wild virtual knot,” “wild equivalence,” or the axiomatics; creating those definitions is itself part of the problem. Also, no ambient ring/field, polynomial variables, homogeneity/degree restrictions, nilpotency assumptions, operator algebra, or phrases such as “for all sufficiently large m” occur here, because the problem is purely topological.
refined_question: In the standard virtual-knot setting of Sections 2.1 and 2.3—where virtual links are represented either by virtual link diagrams modulo the generalized Reidemeister moves or, equivalently, by stable equivalence classes of links embedded in thickened oriented surfaces S_g × R under isotopy, homeomorphisms of the surface, and addition/removal of empty handles—construct a category of “wild virtual knots,” formulate its axiomatics, and prove a theorem characterizing when a wild equivalence between tame virtual links implies that the links are already equivalent in the ordinary tame virtual sense.
equivalent_formulation: Using the surface-embedding model from Theorem 2.1, define a wild analogue of stable equivalence for possibly wild links in thickened oriented surfaces, and characterize when a wild stable equivalence between tame surface embeddings forces ordinary stable equivalence, hence equivalence of the associated virtual link diagrams.
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 18 in Section 8.1 almost verbatim. This paper does not contain a Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3 relevant to the draft; the nearest official formulation is instead the numbered open problem “Wild virtuals.” To make the question fully stand-alone and faithful, one must import the basic setup of virtual knot theory from Sections 2.1 and 2.3, especially the theorem equating virtual-link equivalence with stable equivalence of links in thickened surfaces. No narrower or broader neighboring problem fits the draft as well as Problem 18 does.
